result.topic_en: Direct solution of a pair of trigonometric equations sin(P−A)=k sin(Q−B), sin(P−A')=k' sin(Q−B') by reducing them to tangent equations and rewriting these in exponential (imaginary) form.
result.transcription:
231.
Directe Auflösung der Gleichungen
(1) $\sin(P-A) = k\sin(Q-B)$
(2) $\sin(P-A') = k'\sin(Q-B')$
Es folgt daraus
$\tang\frac{1}{2}(P+Q-A-B) = \frac{k+1}{k-1}\cdot\tang\frac{1}{2}(P-Q-A+B)$
$\tang\frac{1}{2}(P+Q-A'-B') = \frac{k'+1}{k'-1}\cdot\tang\frac{1}{2}(P-Q-A'+B')$
oder wenn wir $\frac{1}{2}(P+Q-A-B) = x$, $\frac{1}{2}(P-Q-A+B) = y$
$\frac{1}{2}(A+B-A'-B') = \alpha$, $\frac{1}{2}(A-B-A'+B') = \beta$, $\frac{k+1}{k-1} = m$, $\frac{k'+1}{k'-1} = n$
setzen
(3) $\tang x = m\tang y$
(4) $\tang(x+\alpha) = n\tang(y+\beta)$
oder in imaginärer Form $\frac{e^{ix}-e^{-ix}}{e^{ix}+e^{-ix}} = m\cdot\frac{e^{iy}-e^{-iy}}{e^{iy}+e^{-iy}}$
oder
$e^{2ix} = \frac{(1+m)e^{iy}+(1-m)e^{-iy}}{(1-m)e^{iy}+(1+m)e^{-iy}}$ und
$e^{2i(x+\alpha)} = \frac{(1+n)e^{i(y+\beta)}+(1-n)e^{-i(y+\beta)}}{(1-n)e^{i(y+\beta)}+(1+n)e^{-i(y+\beta)}}$
folglich
$((1+m)e^{iy}+(1-m)e^{-iy})\cdot((1-n)e^{i(y+\beta)}+(1+n)e^{-i(y+\beta)})e^{i\alpha}$
$= ((1-m)e^{iy}+(1+m)e^{-iy})\cdot((1+n)e^{i(y+\beta)}+(1-n)e^{-i(y+\beta)})e^{-i\alpha}$
oder wenn man entwickelt und mit 2 dividirt

methods.what: Conversion of sin(P−A)=k sin(Q−B) into a tangent relation of half-sums and half-differences (tangent rule)
Substitution reducing the system to two tangent equations
Expressing the tangent equation in exponential (imaginary) form and solving for e^{2ix}
Eliminating x by combining the two exponential expressions into one equation in y
